findings.where: Article specimen: the TV-studio photo caption, the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and the three-item list below it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The rhythm breaks exactly where the brief asked it to hold. The caption sits right on top of the subhead with no space, so the subhead looks like it belongs to the photo rather than starting the next section. The list lines are set much tighter than the body text, so wrapped items like 'Project Cycle.' run into the next bullet. The list's last line almost touches the rule under it.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique, because the brief makes this specimen the proof that image, caption, list and subhead sit on one rhythm without hand-tuning. A reader of Mark's article would also object, because the cramped list and the subhead glued to the caption make the page look unfinished.

findings.where: Article specimen: the red-orange bullets and the red-orange underlined link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: An orange-red colour appears that isn't in the tile's own palette, which says 'Four colours and no accent' and puts links in house blue. Links now come in two colours: blue for 'Play again' and the action, red-orange in the article. The red also reads as a warning colour.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for every tile to be built in the house blue and grey. A visitor would also object, because the same function (a link) looks two different ways, and red next to law content reads as an alert.

findings.where: First screen: the blue field's diagonal stripe pattern and the large ghosted 'PPP' letters behind the heading (desktop, and on phone behind the heading)
findings.fault: The direction's lever is one plain blue field, and the tile's own Texture panel says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient'. Yet the hero has diagonal pinstripes and a giant watermark 'PPP' running behind Mark's line. Both add noise behind the text the visitor is reading, and the watermark looks like a stock-template flourish.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who wants a quiet ground with at most one borrowed detail, and dislikes busyness. The bank official reading the heading would also object, because the watermark letters clash with the heading's own letters and make it look less refined.

findings.where: First screen: the five outlined pills under the lead (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation)
findings.fault: They are static, but each draws a rounded box in the link colour, so they look like buttons or topic filters. Clicking one does nothing. They also put a row of five button-like shapes beside the one real action, against 'one message, one action'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'PPP Law' expecting Mark's PPP writing, gets nothing and is confused. The founder would also object, because the extra row adds clutter to a first screen meant to carry one action.

findings.fault: The page's only action links to '#' and not to a mailto, so clicking the address does nothing. The arrow promises a destination the button doesn't have.
findings.who_objects: The official ready to write, who clicks and nothing happens. They can only copy the address by hand from the button.

findings.fault: The portrait and its caption fill the whole first phone screen. Mark's line, the lead and the email action only appear after a full scroll. On a first look the phone visitor sees a face, a nav and a placeholder caption, with no message and no way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: The bank official opening the link on a phone from LinkedIn or email. In the first five seconds they cannot tell what Mark does or how to reach him.

findings.where: First screen: the lockup 'Mark M. Moseley / Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's name is set small in the corner, after the logo, at about nav size. The logo comes first and the name reads as a caption to it. The brief says his name should lead with the logo beside it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because 'his name leads' is part of the personal-advisor test. The visitor would also object, because they have to work out whose voice the large heading is.

findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen shows evidence of work. No named body asked for his advice, no region or place and year is given, and there is no recent talk. The claim 'I advise multilateral development banks…' stands without any proof next to the action.
findings.who_objects: The senior bank official, who hires against terms of reference and wants to see that Mark has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs, in their region, before writing.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The title is set in a heavy Bold, although the type-pair note says SemiBold for article titles. The apostrophe in 'World's' renders as a straight, typewriter-like mark, while the subhead uses curly quotes.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who wants refined, serious type. A careful legal reader would also notice a heavier-than-specified title and mismatched quote marks.

findings.where: Type pair panel: the 'Source Sans 3' specimen
findings.fault: The sans specimen floats low in the right column. It doesn't line up with the top or the baseline of 'In my view, Gelasio', so the two halves of the pair don't read as a pair.
findings.who_objects: The founder looking at the type pair, because it looks unplaced and makes the panel look careless.
